key_insight: A unified framework pairs a forward predictive model with an inverse generative model to design liquid electrolyte formulations, producing three high‑conductivity candidates that were experimentally validated—demonstrating goal‑directed formulation discovery.
problem_solved: Speeds and focuses electrolyte discovery by bridging property prediction and candidate generation, reducing reliance on slow, trial‑and‑error experimental screening.
method: Train a forward predictive model that maps electrolyte formulations to target properties (e.g., ionic conductivity).
Use an inverse generative model conditioned on desired properties to propose new formulations (goal‑directed generation).
Close the loop with experimental validation of top candidates to confirm predictions and prioritize designs.
impact: Shows a practical, generalizable pattern for combining predictive and generative AI in materials/formulation design; AI/ML practitioners can adapt this unified pipeline to accelerate discovery and reduce experimental cost and time.
visual_elements: Architecture schematic: forward predictor → inverse generator → candidate ranking → experimental loop
Parity plot: predicted vs. measured conductivity highlighting the three validated candidates
Latent‑space or embedding map showing generated candidates clustered near target property region
Workflow timeline/infographic: in silico generation → selection → lab validation (bar chart of measured conductivities)
paper_title: A unified predictive and generative solution for liquid electrolyte formulation
paper_authors: Zhenze Yang, Yifan Wu, Xu Han, Ziqing Zhang, Haoen Lai
